The main takeaway from our work is that

the stereochemistry of the cluster is not fixed and the cluster is not a chiral molecule, but the cluster does have a preferred orientation in solution which is determined by the steric interactions of the ligand with the cluster.
equatorial substituents can slow the rate of epimerization at a cluster center.
turnstile rotations are not always observed, even in clusters with a high number of equatorially coordinated ligands.
